correctness.rationale: For every L>=5, the relative Y formed from centered tetrahedra retracts to the honeycomb graph H_L; only the 2L² alternating color triangles lie outside. Each pair of black/white relative 2-cells has the same facial boundary c_f; the unique integral facial relation is sum_f c_f=0 (fundamental class of torus). Thus H2 is exactly the kernel whose per-face coefficient sums are a single integer, with basis T=sum_f e_f^W and s_f=e_f^B-e_f^W, rank L²+1. The group action follows from orientation and color-exchange signs: g(s_f)=delta*epsilon*s_(gf), g(T)=delta(T+((1-epsilon)/2)S). Translations force a potential equivariant integral section T+aS with a integral; a color-flipping orientation-preserving 60-degree rotation requires 2a=1, impossible, while a=1/2 splits rationally. Coinvariants reduce to 2T=0, 2s=0, L²s=0, giving Z/2 for odd L and (Z/2)^2 for even L; rational invariants in H1,H2 vanish, so the finite quotient is rationally acyclic in positive degrees. The proof explicitly distinguishes algebraic coinvariants from integral homology of the orbit space. The checker sources reconstruct orientations and Smith forms for L=5..8, which are finite corroboration only.
